card.summary: Free compute on fal's inference platform. The eligibility sentence, quoted: 'The fal Research Grants program is open to anyone passionate about advancing AI ...

free_tier.stated: Free compute on fal's inference platform. The eligibility sentence, quoted: 'The fal Research Grants program is open to anyone passionate about advancing AI through open source projects. [...] No formal degree is required - your ideas and dedication are what matter most.' The page states '$50k' as the 'average grant check' and gives no amount for an individual award. The route is an email to grants@fal.ai with a project description, goals, and 'any relevant work or GitHub repositories'.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The grant is platform credit, so it composes only with fal's own models; it is a supplement for an inference-heavy step, not a training allowance. fal Serverless GPU price list on the pricing page, separate from the grant (whether grant credit applies to Serverless GPUs is not stated): H100 80GB at $4.50/h list price and $2.49/h in the 'As low as' column ($0.00125/s and $0.000692/s), billed per second while a runner is alive, with no minimum bill stated; the page does not say what 'As low as' requires. RTX PRO 6000 96GB, H200, B200, GB200 and B300 are listed; A100, L40S, L4 and GeForce cards are not listed.

limits.value: the award has no published amount, cap, duration or expiry, so the only thing bounding it is a discretionary reply to an email.

record.notes: Recorded for the door rather than the number, and it is honest to say so: the page states an average grant of $50k and no per-award amount, so the finding ranks only on the average. What makes it worth a line is the explicit removal of the degree requirement in a class where nearly every other program gates on it, plus the fact that the application is an email rather than a form. The page also states $2m in total grants and two named testimonials. Whether the credits are GPU-seconds on fal's inference endpoints or spend on the platform is not stated, and that distinction decides whether a training run is possible at all - it probably is not, which is the caveat.

card.summary: No published byte quota on the /data volume. The docs state only 'Files written to /data persist between requests, across runner restarts, and across deploym...

free_tier.stated: No published byte quota on the /data volume. The docs state only 'Files written to /data persist between requests, across runner restarts, and across deployments' and 'Files you write there persist until you delete them. Runner shutdown does not delete these files.' Capacity is bounded only by what you pay to keep a runner alive; there is no free storage allowance and no documented ceiling.

retention.stated: No published byte quota on the /data volume. The docs state only 'Files written to /data persist between requests, across runner restarts, and across deployments' and 'Files you write there persist until you delete them.

egress.terms: NOT free and NOT anonymous: '/data' files are 'not URL-accessible'. There is no public download URL, so the egress question does not arise. Bulk in/out is via `fal files` CLI or the REST storage API.

record.tooling: `fal` Python CLI (`fal files upload/download/list/remove`), @fal-ai/client JS storage API, `fal.download_file(url, target_dir='/data/...')` in-app. Chunked at 4 MB into a global object store; parallel reads hit a distributed cache (docs claim 6-8 GB/s distributed, 10-15 GB/s local NVMe).
record.chaining: Storage is tied to paid compute workloads rather than standalone storage. Serverless deployments require approved account access and compute runtime fees apply.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap is upload-method-dependent (this is the useful part): `fal files upload` CLI ~100 GB per file (10 MB parts, max 10,000 parts); dashboard drag-and-drop 1 GB; upload-from-URL 5 GB and must complete in 10 minutes; POST /serverless/files/file/local/{path} ~4.5 MB per request; writes from inside a running app are exempt ('Not subject to these limits. The runner writes straight to the volume'). Retention: indefinite, self-managed. Billing: you are billed per second for every runner state except PENDING, DOCKER_PULL and TERMINATED. SETUP and IDLE are both billed, so holding storage open costs GPU-time.
record.reliability_note: Serverless access is gated by per-account approval (request at fal.ai/dashboard/serverless-get-started), so this is not a self-serve multiplier. Docs warn that streaming a multi-GB artifact in small chunks to /data is much slower than one bulk copy.

evidence.proved: 'Files written to /data persist between requests, across runner restarts, and across deployments'; no quota stated
